reason: Real defect: §3 carefully hedges 5.6 TB/s vs 3.35 TB/s as an aggregate, deliberately-hypothetical single-device illustration, but §5 Common Mistakes and §8 mini-case restate the same comparison with no hedge, so a reader can conclude the canonical 8xH100 host misses its 25 ms TPOT - which is false (per-GPU shard needs 700 GB/s = 20.9% of peak). NOTE: the reviewer's own 'weight read binds until B = 295' is miscalculated - 2N = 1.4e11 FLOP/token, not 1.75e10, giving B = 5.22ms/0.1416ms = 37, not 295.
evidence: chapter-02.md:115 (§3, hedged) 'Read this as an *aggregate lower-bound illustration*, not as the literal bandwidth requirement of a single H100 in a realistic 8xH100 configuration (where the model and its traffic are sharded ...)'; :109 '(A 140-GB FP16 model cannot reside on a single 80-GB H100 anyway, so the whole-model-on-one-GPU comparison is deliberately hypothetical.)'. :147 (§5, UNhedged) 'a single H100 cannot meet the decode bandwidth demand (5.6 TB/s vs 3.35 TB/s)'. :177 (§8, UNhedged) 'decode will be bandwidth-bound (a ~140 GB/token weight-read requiring ~5.6 TB/s sustained over each ~25 ms decode step)'. python: 70e9/8*2 = 17.5 GB/GPU; 17.5/0.025 = 700 GB/s; 700/3350 = 20.90%; 17.5/3350*1000 = 5.22 ms; 2*70e9/0.989e15*1000 = 0.1416 ms/token; 5.22/0.1416 = 36.9 (B = 37, NOT 295).
